name: mta-audit
problem: Attribution models always return an answer. Almost none report whether that answer survives a small change in assumptions, so teams act on campaign rankings that may not hold.
architecture: A Python package that takes journey-level event data, resamples whole journeys rather than rows, and runs a battery of stability checks across conversion windows, identity stitching, touchpoint loss, and model choice. Score weights are published as policy with a sensitivity report.
decisions: Resample whole journeys, never individual rows, so the unit of resampling matches the unit of analysis.
Publish score weights as stated policy rather than burying them, and ship a sensitivity report alongside.
Report when the data cannot support a call instead of returning a number regardless.
testing: Tested against the public Criteo attribution dataset with injected faults, plus a CI suite across three Python versions.
evaluation: On an 8,000-user Criteo sample, injected duplicate events of 1 to 10 percent were detected on every run and moved the data-quality score from 72 to roughly 50.
deployment: Published to PyPI; installable with pip.
limitations: It measures stability, not causal lift. It does not replace an incrementality test.

name: Governed AI data access over MCP
problem: Analysts wanted AI-assisted access to enterprise data without handing a model unrestricted query rights against production warehouses.
architecture: Custom Model Context Protocol servers exposing Snowflake, S3, and Hive to an AI-native development workflow, with validation and enforced limits between the model and the data.
decisions: Validate generated SQL and HiveQL before execution rather than trusting model output.
Enforce row limits and injection prevention at the server, not in the prompt.
Authenticate through enterprise SSO so access follows existing identity.
testing: Validated against production query patterns in use by analytics teams.
evaluation: Adopted by analytics users for day-to-day work; direct HiveServer2 connectivity and Parquet-native reads roughly doubled Hive analysis throughput.
limitations: Employer work, so there is no public code or data. I can walk through the design and the threat model in an interview.

name: Agent reliability study
problem: When a scoring model picks an agent's best attempt, a large share of the picks are broken. The question is whether a second opinion catches them.
architecture: A pre-registered offline evaluation over two software-engineering benchmarks, with the projects' real test suites as ground truth.
decisions: Register the population, the metric, and the stopping rule before any outcome data existed.
Evaluate on the population the selector actually commits, not on the candidate pool.
Keep a model-free baseline in the comparison and let it win if it wins.
testing: Executed test suites decided every label; oracle controls were run before any model output was graded.
evaluation: Reported in the write-up, which is under anonymous review.
limitations: The write-up is under anonymous workshop review, so the details are off this site until reviews return.

name: SIGNAL
problem: A consumer investor wants to know whether to hold a position over the next quarter. The honest answer depends on valuation, momentum, risk, balance sheet and macro at once, plus whatever the filings say. Reading all of that is the barrier, and most tools answer by producing one confident number that hides its own uncertainty.
architecture: Two engines behind one answer-first interface. A quick read computes a deterministic weighting of six checks from live market data in the browser, with no model involved. The canonical engine is a Python research system: an evidence agent pulls prices, key statistics, SEC filing text and an optional macro series; a quant score is computed in pure code and versioned; bull and bear memos are written by a model through a single OpenRouter module; a synthesis produces one view with kill criteria; and a code-only critic checks every claim against its cited source. Disagreement between the quant band and the narrative lean is built in code and published as a first-class object rather than averaged away.
decisions: The quant score is a pure function computed in code, and the language-model layer cannot import it. An eval feeds hostile model output that tries to set the score and asserts the persisted value does not move.
Exactly one module holds the model key, base URL, retries, backoff and JSON repair, so there is a single place where model access can be audited or swapped.
Disagreement between the quantitative band and the narrative lean is computed in code and shown, with reasons each side could be wrong. Agreement is not required for a valid run.

Every claim is labelled sourced, inference or unsupported and carries source ids, and a deterministic critic reports the share of confident claims that are actually cited plus any citation pointing at nothing.
Missing inputs drop out of the weighted sum and are flagged, rather than being scored as zero, so absent data cannot read as neutral evidence.
No LangGraph. The pipeline is an ordered Python function because nothing yet needs graph-shaped branching or retries.
testing: Six test modules run with no network through a mocked model transport, covering the quant formula, the pipeline, the model client and the evaluation suite. Thirteen eval cases bind by id to specific checks, including three that prove the model cannot set or adjust the score.
evaluation: The evaluation suite and the mocked tests pass. A prediction log has accumulated 154 runs across 15 tickers on a three-month horizon, recording the quant score, band, narrative lean, agreement and entry price for each. Those predictions are not yet scored against realised outcomes, so the system has a structural argument for trustworthiness and no track record yet.
deployment: Static front end on GitHub Pages. A scheduled workflow runs the research export each weekday evening for the tickers on the watchlist and commits the results and the prediction log back to the repository, which is how calibration survives an ephemeral runner. A Cloudflare Worker proxies market data so no key ships in the bundle.
limitations: Full research is published only for the eight tickers on the watchlist; any other ticker falls back to the browser-side quick read. The narrative lean has come back mixed in 142 of 154 logged runs, so the disagreement feature rarely fires with real force. Predictions are logged but not yet resolved, so there is no accuracy claim. Peer valuation, user-supplied documents as evidence, and portfolio-level effects are not built. The advanced terminal is the original design prototype with illustrative numbers and is labelled as such.

name: Integrated Marketing Attribution (IMA)
problem: Mix models see the whole budget but only at channel level, while attribution sees individual paths and degrades as privacy rules remove identifiers. The framework ties the two together so granular reads stay consistent with the mix model without user-level tracking.
architecture: Bayesian decomposition that splits channel-level contribution into campaigns and placements with uncertainty, anchored so the granular estimates reconcile with the marketing mix model. Implementing a published framework, not inventing one.
decisions: Anchor the granular estimates to the mix model so the two cannot disagree arithmetically.
Give small campaigns priors that regularise without drowning the data.
Keep the output checkable by people who will never read the model.
testing: Validation diagnostics against the mix model's channel totals.
evaluation: Employer work in progress; no public results.
limitations: Employer work, so there is no public code, data or metrics here. I did not write the paper; my part is turning it into working code. I can walk through the method and the design choices in an interview.
